query: What signals in a travel-expense description predict whether it will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_type_category
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, interpretable categories (hardware, travel_service, software) that a human can segment on and compare decline rates across. Associational, not a restatement of decline state.

per_column.name: expense_mechanism
per_column.rationale: How the expense was created (automated vs manual vs procurement) is a plausible, interpretable driver of approval outcome and gives clean segments to compare against declines.

per_column.name: travel_relevance
per_column.rationale: Clean binary split (travel vs not) directly relevant to a travel-expense decline query; easy to group and compare, though coarse.

per_column.name: purchase_intent_signal
per_column.rationale: Interpretable action categories (new_acquisition, registration, upgrade) that could plausibly associate with decline likelihood and support segmentation.

per_column.name: department_requestor
per_column.rationale: Interpretable and segmentable, but the original table already contains 'department'; this largely duplicates existing information rather than opening a new relationship.

per_column.name: source_system_tracking
per_column.rationale: Opaque boolean flag with unclear meaning; near-binary but its semantic link to decline is not interpretable, offering little explanatory grouping value.

per_column.name: asset_specificity
per_column.rationale: Specific_model vs generic_placeholder is an interpretable data-quality signal that plausibly relates to declines (vague descriptions rejected); good segmentation.

per_column.name: hardware_device_class
per_column.rationale: Interpretable device categories, though heavily NULL for non-hardware rows and partially overlapping asset_type_category; still allows meaningful comparison within hardware.

judge.rationale: Most columns are interpretable, well-separated categorical variables that a human can segment on and compare against decline rates, satisfying the EDA claim. asset_type_category, expense_mechanism, travel_relevance, purchase_intent_signal, and asset_specificity are the strongest, offering distinct, meaningful groupings. Weaknesses: department_requestor duplicates the existing 'department' column (restatement), source_system_tracking is an opaque flag with unclear semantics, and there is notable redundancy among the asset-oriented columns (asset_type_category, hardware_device_class, purchase_intent_signal). The set skews toward asset/procurement framing rather than travel-expense-description signals implied by the query, capping overall informativeness at moderate.
